title: Knee Rebuild: Full-Body Program

operatingRules.intro: Every session is a load test and the knee's 24-hour response is the inspection report: progress when the report is clean twice running, hold when it's noisy, back off when it's bad. The phase dates are estimates; the gates decide.

signals.clean: 3 or under, not climbing set to set
signals.backOff: Over 5, or sharp pain on the joint line: stop the exercise

signals.clean: Back to baseline; stiffness gone within 30 min
signals.hold: Stiffer or sorer than the day before, clears within the day
signals.backOff: Visible swelling, warmth, or pain up 2+ points

signals.clean: Each session as good as or better than the last
signals.backOff: Two off sessions in a row

triggers: Clean twice in a row: progress that exercise one notch — load, range, step height, or the single-leg version.
Hold: repeat the last session's loads exactly.

Back off: cut that exercise's load 20–30% or step back to its earlier version. If the whole knee is complaining, the next run becomes an elliptical session and the next lift's lower-body work runs at Phase 1 loads.
loading: Double progression. Pick the rep range (say 8–12). When every set hits the top of the range at RPE 8 or under, add the smallest increment (5 lb per dumbbell, one plate on a stack, 10 lb on the Smith) and start again at the bottom. RPE 8 means two reps left in the tank.
Lower body starts at RPE 6 in Phase 1 and reaches RPE 8 on the main lifts by Phase 3. Upper body runs RPE 7–9 from day one.
The injured leg goes first on every single-leg exercise and sets the rep count for the other side. Symmetry is the goal, so the healthy leg doesn't get to run ahead.
Any exercise can be swapped for one on the same row of the substitutions table at the end; the slot's job stays the same.

Weeks 4, 8 and 12 are deloads: lifting sets down by a third at the same loads, with the mileage down weeks landing on the same weeks. Weeks 4 and 8 are also Thanksgiving and Christmas weeks, so the easy weeks fall where life gets busy anyway.

weeklyTemplateNote: Running the day after a lift is deliberate: easy runs on tired legs are low risk, and the layout keeps Sunday completely off. If the knee flares on this schedule, stack instead: lift and run on the same day (lift first, easy run or elliptical after), which buys a second full rest day. Sprint coaches call that high/low; stack the stress, then rest hard.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.summary: Three machine-dominant full-body sessions that re-teach the knee to take load through a pain-free range while the upper body trains hard. Lower-body work starts at RPE 6 and earns its way to 7; feeling under-challenged for two weeks is the design, not a bug.
notes: If you're already leg-pressing and squatting pain-free, treat Phase 1 as a two-week calibration and move on once Gate 1 is clean. Warm-up first (see the warm-up section), then:
Progression inside the phase: Add 5–10 lb when the top of a rep range is clean twice.
Step height goes up 2 in. once 3 × 10 with 20 lb dumbbells is clean.
Balance progresses from eyes open to eyes closed, then onto a folded mat.

phases.name: Single-leg strength and balance
phases.summary: Same A/B/C skeleton and the same upper-body progression; the lower-body slots trade two-legged machine work for the single-leg patterns running and lacrosse are built on. Loads move from RPE 6–7 to 7–8 across the four weeks.
notes: Week 4 is a deload, which makes it the right week to learn the new movements: light loads, perfect reps, and Thanksgiving in the middle of it.
Everything not listed (the pressing, pulling, carries and core) carries over from Phase 1 with double progression.

From week 6, add landing prep at the start of sessions A and C: snap-downs, 3 × 5. Stand tall, drop into an athletic stance and freeze for 2 s. No jump yet; this is the absorbing half, taught before the exploding half.

phases.name: Power, deceleration and lacrosse prep
phases.summary: Plyometrics enter at the front of sessions A and C, the main lower lifts move to heavier sets of 6–8, and strides return to one run a week. Order inside a session matters: hops while fresh, then strength, then anything that burns.
notes: Landing rules: every landing is quiet and stuck, about 40 ground contacts a session is plenty at this stage, and a loud landing or a knee that caves inward ends the set.
Upper: Structure unchanged; keep running double progression. Add a fourth upper slot (face pulls or the rear-delt machine) if sessions finish under 55 minutes

Running in Phase 3: from week 8, finish Wednesday's run with 4 × 15 s strides building to about 85% effort, full walk-back between. From week 10, if Gate 2 was clean, Friday's run carries a 2 × 5 min comfortably-hard segment with 3 min easy between.

phases.name: Lacrosse
phases.summary: Phase 4 preview, week 13 on, a week or two per rung with the same clean-twice rule.
notes: When Gate 3 is clean, I'll write Phase 4 in this same format.

redFlagsIntro: Any of these means the session is over and the next call is to the ortho or PT, not a Hold and another try on Thursday.

redFlags.text: Swelling that shows up within hours of a session and isn't gone in 48 hours
The knee giving way, buckling, or a shifting sensation under load
Locking or catching: a mechanical block to straightening or bending
Sharp pain on the joint line, or pain that wakes you at night
Range of motion worse than it was the week before
Pain climbing session over session despite two back-offs
Numbness or tingling below the knee

notFlags: Not flags: mild stiffness for the first 10 minutes, ordinary quad and glute soreness 24–48 hours after a new movement, and a knee that complains at the top of the stairs the day after Bulgarians.

lift.intro: Every lift opens with 5 minutes on the upright bike and a 5-minute knee circuit; the circuit is non-negotiable in Phase 1 and shrinks to 3 minutes once the plyos arrive in Phase 3.
lift.bike: Bike setup: seat high enough that the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke, easy resistance, no standing.
circuit: Terminal knee extensions with the mini band (or the cable and ankle strap), 2 × 15. Band behind the knee, straighten against it; this wakes up the quad.
Glute bridge, 2 × 10 with a 2 s hold at the top.
Lateral band walks, 2 × 10 steps each way.
Bodyweight split squat through a partial range, 2 × 8 each leg.
Leg swings, front-to-back and side-to-side, 10 each, with a hand on the Smith upright.
Knee-to-wall ankle rocks, 10 each side; your existing ankle work carries straight over.

warmUp.run: Before a run: 3–5 minutes of walking, then the leg swings and 10 bodyweight squats to a comfortable depth.
offDays: Keep the thoracic, hip and ankle routine you already run.
Add a 2 × 60 s couch stretch for the hip flexors and a 2 × 45 s calf stretch each side.
If the knee doesn't fully straighten yet, add a heel prop, 3 × 2 min with the heel on a rolled towel and the knee hanging; full extension matters more than full bend for running.
recovery: Ice for 10–15 minutes only if there's swelling; otherwise skip it.
Sleep is the recovery variable that moves everything else. Protein around 0.7–1 g per pound of bodyweight supports the tissue work.
Deload weeks 4, 8 and 12: lifting sets down a third at the same loads, mileage down as charted in the running section.
If you use the stacked layout, the run after a lift is easy only.

running.intro: Three runs a week, weekly mileage from 10 to 18 by week 11 with a down week every fourth, and almost all of it easy. Your engine came through the layoff fine (the watch read a VO2 max estimate of 55 on Sep 28); the chassis is what's still being re-welded, so volume follows the knee, not your lungs.
rules: Weeks 4, 8 and 12 drop back to let the knee consolidate, then the build resumes from a higher floor.
The long run is at most 40% of the week's miles and grows about half a mile a week; the other two runs split the rest.
Monday's MBR stays social and easy, Wednesday is the flat easy run, Friday is the long one.
80/20: Phase 1 is all easy. One faster Friday every other week from Phase 2; strides and a short tempo arrive in Phase 3 as written there. The Oct 23 effort is the kind of run to ration, not ban.
The weekly number is a ceiling, not a quota. Knee clean: take it. Knee on Hold: repeat last week's.

Swap any run for 30–40 minutes of elliptical or rower at the same effort when the knee says Hold; it costs nothing aerobically and spares the joint. On the rower, strap in, drive with the legs only through the pain-free range, and keep the stroke rate around 22–24.
Stair climber: 5 slow minutes as a warm-up at most in Phases 1–2. It's a lot of loaded knee bending for the payoff.
Treadmill at 1% incline when footing or weather is bad; the belt is the one place you control the terrain.
running.phase3: Running in Phase 3: from week 8, finish Wednesday's run with 4 × 15 s strides building to about 85% effort, full walk-back between. From week 10, if Gate 2 was clean, Friday's run carries a 2 × 5 min comfortably-hard segment with 3 min easy between.

strides.text: 4 × 15 s strides building to about 85% effort, full walk-back between

tempo.text: 2 × 5 min comfortably-hard segment with 3 min easy between

fasterFriday.text: One faster effort every other Friday from Phase 2 on

setupNotes: Smith machine: the bar path is fixed, so set your feet 6–12 in. ahead of the bar for squats to keep the shins near vertical, and directly under it for RDLs. Set the safety stops every time. The bar's own weight varies by machine (usually 15–25 lb); ignore it and track plates.
Leg press: on the seated machine, set the seat so the knees start at about 90°. Feet high on the platform shifts the work toward glutes and hamstrings and reduces shear at the knee.
Step platforms: the 30-minute circuit's aerobic steps stack in roughly 2 in. risers; borrow one when the circuit isn't running. A flat bench is 17–18 in., which is Phase 2 height at the earliest.
Nordic negatives: lat pulldown thigh pad at its lowest notch, kneel facing away with heels tucked under it, a mat under the knees. The back extension bench's foot plates work too.
Hop tests: two strips of tape on the floor, a tape measure, best of three per leg, a minute between legs. Test fresh, before lifting, on the same day of the week each time.
Dumbbells cap at 75 lb (60 at some clubs). When RDLs or carries outgrow the rack: single-leg RDL, a 4 s lowering, or the Smith machine RDL; carries become suitcase carries with one dumbbell.
Dropping anything trips the lunk alarm; the Smith RDL is the legal deadlift.
